nodes.summary: The abstraction `[a]x`.
nodes.title: Abstraction of an element at a bound atom

nodes.summary: Equality of abstractions is α-equivalence.
nodes.title: Equality of abstractions is α-equivalence

nodes.summary: An abstraction with the same bound atom determines its body.
nodes.title: Abstractions with the same bound atom have equal bodies

nodes.summary: Reflexivity of α-equivalence. α-equivalence is reflexive.
nodes.title: Reflexivity of α-equivalence

nodes.summary: Symmetry of α-equivalence. α-equivalence is symmetric. Symmetry uses equivariance of support (`supp_smul`).
nodes.title: Symmetry of α-equivalence

nodes.summary: Transitivity of α-equivalence. α-equivalence is transitive. Transitivity uses the fact that two permutations agreeing on `supp y` act equally on `y` (`smul_eq_of_agree_on_supp`).
nodes.title: Transitivity of α-equivalence

nodes.summary: α-equivalence relation on atom–element pairs. α-equivalence: equal pairs, or a renaming of the bound atom by a fresh transposition.
nodes.title: α-equivalence relation on atom–element pairs

nodes.summary: The setoid of α-equivalence.
nodes.title: Setoid of α-equivalence

nodes.summary: The action of a permutation on abstractions, applied to a representative.
nodes.title: Permutation action on abstractions

nodes.summary: Atom abstraction: `[a]x`, the quotient of `Atom × X` by α-equivalence.
nodes.title: Atom abstraction of a nominal set

nodes.summary: Every element has a fresh atom: choose one outside any of its supports.
nodes.title: Existence of fresh atoms

nodes.summary: A least finite support exists: among the supports of `x`, one is contained in every support. The proof is by strong induction on a chosen support `S₀`: either every element of `S₀` lies in every support (so `S₀` itself is least), or some `a ∈ S₀` is missing from a support `Sₐ`, and the induction hypothesis applies to the strictly smaller support `Sₐ ∩ S₀`.
nodes.title: Existence of a least finite support

nodes.summary: The subgroup of finitely supported permutations of `Atom`: permutations that fix all atoms outside some finite set.
nodes.title: Subgroup of finitely supported permutations of atoms

nodes.summary: The group of finitely supported permutations of `Atom`.
nodes.title: Group of finitely supported permutations

nodes.summary: Freshness is exactly non-membership in the least support.
nodes.title: Freshness is non-membership in the least support

nodes.summary: `a` is *fresh* for `x`, written `a # x` in the nominal literature, when some finite support of `x` does not contain `a`.
nodes.title: Freshness of an atom for an element

nodes.summary: A permutation moves a support of `x` to a support of `π • x`.
nodes.title: Permutation image of a support

nodes.summary: The intersection of two supports is a support: a permutation fixing the intersection fixes `x`, since every atom it can move (outside some finite support of the permutation, and outside the intersection) is fresh for `x`.
nodes.title: Intersection of two supports is a support

nodes.summary: An element fixed by every permutation has the empty set as a support.
nodes.title: Equivariant elements of a nominal set

nodes.summary: Membership in the least support: `a ∈ supp (Atom := Atom) x` iff `a` lies in every support of `x`.
nodes.title: Membership in the least support

nodes.summary: A support can be enlarged: fixing a larger set pointwise is a stronger hypothesis.
nodes.title: Enlarging a support

nodes.summary: A type with an action of finite permutations in which every element has a finite support: a *nominal set*.
nodes.title: Nominal set

nodes.summary: A pair is supported by the union of supports of its components.
nodes.title: A pair is supported by the union of its components' supports

nodes.summary: A permutation applied to an abstraction, on representatives.
nodes.title: Permutation action on abstractions computed on representatives

nodes.summary: Two permutations that agree on the support of `x` act equally on `x`: their ratio fixes the support pointwise, hence fixes `x`.
nodes.title: Permutations agreeing on the support act equally

nodes.summary: A permutation that fixes every atom outside a finite set `F` of fresh atoms fixes `x`, by induction on `F`. If `π a = a` we apply the induction hypothesis to `π`; otherwise we factor `π = swap a b * π'` with `b = π a`, where `π'` fixes `a` and has support inside `F \ {a}`, and `swap a b` fixes `x` since `a` and `b` are fresh.
nodes.title: Permutations moving only fresh atoms fix the element

nodes.summary: The support of an abstraction is the body's support minus the bound atom.
nodes.title: Support of an atom abstraction

nodes.summary: The support of an atom is its singleton.
nodes.title: Support of an atom

nodes.summary: An equivariant element has empty support.
nodes.title: Equivariant elements have empty support

nodes.summary: Support is equivariant: permuting `x` permutes its support.
nodes.title: Equivariance of the least support

nodes.summary: The least support is contained in every support: minimality.
nodes.title: Minimality of the least support

nodes.summary: The least support is a support.
nodes.title: Least support is a support

nodes.summary: The *least* finite support of `x`: a support contained in every support of `x`.
nodes.title: Least finite support of an element

nodes.summary: An equivariant element is supported by the empty set.
nodes.title: Equivariant elements are supported by the empty set

nodes.summary: The action of a permutation on an abstraction fixes it when the permutation fixes `supp x \ {a}` pointwise.
nodes.title: Abstractions are supported by the body's support minus the atom

nodes.summary: `S` supports `x` when every finite permutation fixing `S` pointwise fixes `x`.
nodes.title: Supporting set of atoms for an element

nodes.summary: Transpositions are symmetric.
nodes.title: Symmetry of transpositions

nodes.summary: Conjugation of a transposition: `σ * swap b c * σ⁻¹ = swap (σ b) (σ c)`.
nodes.title: Conjugation of a transposition

nodes.summary: A transposition is its own inverse.
nodes.title: A transposition is its own inverse

nodes.summary: A transposition is an involution, stated for the `FinPerm` group.
nodes.title: A transposition squares to the identity

nodes.summary: A transposition of an atom with itself is the identity.
nodes.title: Transposition of an atom with itself is the identity

nodes.summary: Swapping two fresh atoms fixes `x`. The proof uses a third atom `c` fresh for both witnessing supports, and the conjugation identity `swap a b = swap a c * swap b c * swap a c`.
nodes.title: Swapping two fresh atoms fixes the element

nodes.summary: A transposition fixes every atom distinct from its two swapped atoms.
nodes.title: Transposition fixes atoms other than the swapped pair

nodes.summary: A transposition of two atoms both outside a support of `x` fixes `x`.
nodes.title: Transposition of atoms outside a support fixes the element

nodes.summary: Applying a transposition is applying the underlying `Equiv.swap`.
nodes.title: Action of a transposition

nodes.summary: The transposition of two atoms, as a finite permutation.
nodes.title: Transposition of two atoms

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
